edges.description: Susceptibility variants alter thalamic T-type calcium channel behavior.
Susceptibility variants alter GABA-A receptor-mediated thalamic inhibition.
Rebound burst firing drives synchronized thalamocortical oscillation.
Slow GABAergic hyperpolarization de-inactivates T-type calcium channels, enabling rebound bursting in relay neurons.
Thalamocortical hypersynchrony produces generalized spike-wave discharges.

In a minority of children the same generalized network hypersynchrony also manifests as a bilateral tonic-clonic seizure rather than only as an absence. This edge rests on the shared idiopathic generalized epilepsy substrate that this node conforms to, not on a separately evidenced step.
Generalized spike-wave discharges produce the clinical absence seizure.
The discharge modelled by this node is what the clinical EEG records.
The clinical absence seizure of this syndrome: abrupt behavioural arrest with impaired awareness and no post-ictal confusion.
The absence seizure is generalized at onset, which is the seizure-type classification this phenotype records.
Reduced GLUT1 transporter function lowers cerebrospinal fluid glucose, the diagnostic read-out of this subset.

nodes.description: GABAergic neurons of the thalamic reticular nucleus provide inhibition onto thalamic relay neurons. Excessive or mistimed GABA-mediated inhibition (including GABA-B-mediated slow hyperpolarization) de-inactivates T-type calcium channels, priming relay neurons for rebound bursts. This node captures the single concept of the pro-oscillatory inhibitory input.

nodes.description: Low-threshold (T-type) calcium currents in thalamic relay and reticular neurons promote low-threshold calcium spikes and rebound burst firing. An enhanced or dysregulated T-type current lowers the threshold for the rhythmic bursting that underlies spike-wave oscillation. This node captures the single concept of the pro-oscillatory calcium current.

nodes.description: CAE has a strong genetic basis that is usually complex (polygenic) rather than single-gene. Variants affecting thalamic T-type calcium channels (e.g., CACNA1H) and GABA-A receptor subunits (e.g., GABRG2, GABRB3) shift the excitation-inhibition balance of the thalamocortical circuit toward abnormal oscillation. This node captures the single concept of the predisposing genetic variation.

nodes.description: A minority of children presenting with absence epilepsy, especially with onset before four years, have GLUT1 deficiency from SLC2A1 variants that reduce protein function. SLC2A1 encodes the GLUT1 glucose transporter, and the clinical read-out of its reduced function is low cerebrospinal fluid glucose. This is a separate mechanism from the thalamocortical channel and receptor nodes of this entry, and it is the reason the subset matters clinically: the ketogenic diet is effective in GLUT1 deficiency. The steps between reduced transporter function and the seizure are not modelled here, because the sources cited state none - in particular, neither of them describes the transport route or an energy-deficit mechanism, so this node asserts the activity decrease and its laboratory consequence and nothing more.
